inCorpusNuggets.author: Richard Campagna
inCorpusNuggets.text: We had the pleasure of staying at the The Phoenician last month and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. The resort itself is aesthetically beautiful, with an impressive range of activities and spaces for both families and adults. Multiple pools, several restaurants, recreational options, and quiet nooks throughout the property make it a destination where n...
inCorpusNuggets.sourceText:
We had the pleasure of staying at the The Phoenician last month and thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

The resort itself is aesthetically beautiful, with an impressive range of activities and spaces for both families and adults. Multiple pools, several restaurants, recreational options, and quiet nooks throughout the property make it a destination where nearly everyone can find a place to relax.

What stood out most, however, was the service, particularly at check-in. Christian noticed that we shared a somewhat uncommon last name and took a few extra moments to genuinely get to know us. He made the arrival process effortless, but what happened later truly surprised us. When we returned to our room that evening, we found a heartfelt handwritten welcome note along with special snacks and a thoughtfully prepared margarita cocktail ensemble.

That level of personalization is increasingly rare today, especially in an era where staffing shortages often leave guests feeling rushed through transactional interactions. Experiences like this are a reminder that service is personal and meaningful, and that organizations capable of delivering it consistently likely invest well in their people and culture.

The rooms were well-appointed, the beds comfortable, and the bathrooms spacious and functional. As someone who admittedly notices details like water pressure, I can report that it was more than adequate. The on-site restaurants offered a nice variety of options, and the servers throughout the resort clearly understood what genuine hospitality looks like. The Tavern in particular was lively and enjoyable, with good live music and excellent service.

A couple of practical notes for future guests: reservations are highly recommended for the restaurants. The seating process can feel a bit cumbersome, with multiple hand-offs even during slower periods. Additionally, poolside service could be more attentive at times, as we occasionally needed to flag staff down.

That said, those issues were minor compared to the overall experience. While five stars may feel slightly generous given the price point and a few operational inefficiencies, on a 1–10 scale this resort is a very solid 9/10 and absolutely worthy of consideration for anyone visiting Scottsdale.

inCorpusNuggets.sourceText:
Attention any families with young kids wanting to come here:
The rooms are not luxury at all and disgusting. The carpet is from 30 years ago and the rooms haven’t been updated probably since. The outdoor patio furniture is old and stained and the floor is GROSS. The coffee machine in here is an old Kerig (most luxury marriot properties have Nespresso). Oh and there’s no complimentary coffee anywhere. You have to go all the way down to the breakfast restaurant to even find it on property. One morning my husband had to buy from their marketplace because the basement coffee wasn’t available and he spent $19 for two regular coffees. Two!

There is nothing to accommodate little kids. The four seasons gave us little stuffed animals and mini robes. Here, nothing. The kids club have a couple random activities for older kids at random times (mainly during nap time).

The customer service is abysmal. I asked a server for a glass so I can have some juice at the buffet I was paying for and he said I should go back to my table and get it myself…. The servers at the pool were rude too and don’t act like an even 3 star resort.

The food on property is also horrendous. All claiming to be high end and luxury but it is anything but. Room service, terrible. The pool food is decent but it takes an hour to receive it. There’s no fast casual place to pick up food for little kids. We had to drive off property most days.

The pool area was also atrocious. There barely were any attendants helping with towels, you have to hunt them down. No one cleans up, there’s trash everywhere and all of the chairs are gross and stained. There was also trash all over the resort.

They also don’t comp parking if you are staying at the resort, which just feels like another way they can squeeze every last dollar from you.

For the amount of money we are spending here it’s a huge disappointment. Next time I’ll stay at a four seasons or the ritz for these prices.

Oh and a sandwich at their “marketplace” was $20 for one! Highway robbery!

Also worth noting we are lifetime gold members and they didn’t do anything for us either.

inCorpusNuggets.sourceText:
A Beautiful Stay with Room for Improvement

The Phoenician Resort is undeniably stunning, from the breathtaking mountain views near our hotel room to the beautifully landscaped grounds, multiple pool options, and towering palm trees that truly make the resort feel like a desert oasis. However, while the scenery impressed us, several aspects of our stay fell short, especially when compared to other top resorts in the Phoenix area.

Dining & Amenities:
One major concern was the limited dining hours. Most on-site restaurants closed by 5:00 PM, with The Tavern being the only option open until 8:00 PM. As out-of-town guests, this left us with little choice in the evenings aside from room service or ordering out. We expected more flexibility and variety in a luxury resort.

Shops & Pool Experience:
All shops on the property also closed early at 5:00 PM, and pool amenities, including the water slide, music, bar, and even the water fountains, were shut down around the same time. This was disappointing, as the pool is typically a hub of activity and relaxation, especially in the summer.

Children's Activities:
We were especially let down by the Funicians Kids Club, which was never open during our stay. This was a major reason we selected the Phoenician, and our children were incredibly disappointed by its unavailability.

Summer Activities:
We appreciated the advertised “Legendary Summers” theme, but there were no events scheduled during the weekdays only on the weekends. Other Phoenix-area resorts we’ve visited provide daily family-friendly activities all summer long, so the lack of weekday activities was a letdown.

Overall, while the resort is visually impressive and offers a serene setting, we felt the guest experience didn’t fully match the high rating and reputation. With a few key improvements especially around extended hours, family activities, and consistent activites the Phoenician could offer a truly legendary experience to match its branding.

Stayed at the Phoenician over the Labor Day weekend. Purchased 2 casitas for my family and my sisters family to celebrate the holiday weekend and our recent birthdays. Around 10 pm at night I noticed the water filling the sink and the bath tub were yellow tinted and dirty. Fortunately the front desk was able to move us to another room that was across a parking lot. Needing to rebath my children and myself we packed up our room, and carried our sleeping children to the new room.
When checking out the front desk manager was rude and since we had booked our rooms with Expedia, a third party, he was unable to make any consessions towards that rooms cost for the evening. I am not the type to complain about the few issues we encountered while staying at the property, but I was very surprised by the lack of courtesy the front desk manager had for our dirty water room, late night packing, moving rooms and my daughter becoming very upset that something was wrong with our room that could not be fixed. I am so disgusted by the fact that my family bathed, washed our face, brushed our teeth with dirty water at this resort. Our primary vacation due to my work, is staycation.... there is not a resort in Scottsdale/Phoenix/Tucson that we have not stayed at 5-3 stars.... skip this resort and go to the Hyatt at Gainey Ranch.... same family fun and entertainment.... clean water...

There are A LOT of stairs to go every where on property. Be prepared!

Wonderful athletic center and spa, if you’re so inclined.
